Employment type: Full time


At Globant, we are working to make the world a better place, one step at a time. We enhance business development and enterprise solutions to prepare them for a digital future. With a diverse and talented team present in more than 30 countries, we are strategic partners to leading global companies in their business process transformation.


We seek a Sr DevOps Engineer / Site Reliability Engineer (SRE) with deep expertise in Azure cloud infrastructure and AI-assisted automation who shares our passion for innovation and change. This role is critical to helping our business partners evolve and adapt to consumers' personalized expectations in this new technological era.


Job Description

In this role, you will build, automate, and run secure, resilient, multi-region infrastructure on Microsoft Azure. You will own the full lifecycle of cloud operations—from infrastructure provisioning to observability—while leveraging AI coding agents to accelerate delivery, streamline workflows, and optimize incident troubleshooting.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Architecting Azure networking solutions, including VNets, subnets, peering, private endpoints, Network Security Groups (NSGs), and DNS.
  • Implementing global and multi-region deployments engineered for high availability and disaster recovery.
  • Owning end-to-end observability, including monitoring, alerting, Service Level Objectives (SLOs), incident response, and root-cause analysis.

title: Senior Compliance Specialist
description:
AtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 33 million people worldwide. Electrophysiologists and cardiothoracic surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib and reduction of Afib related complications. AtriCure’s Isolator® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE® probe is cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac and thoracic procedures. For more information, visit AtriCure.com or follow us on LinkedIn.

We foster a culture of inclusion by embracing diverse experiences and individuals where everyone’s authentic self is welcome. We offer supporting programs and resources that provide enriching and equitable opportunities for each person to contribute professionally and personally.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The APAC Senior Compliance Specialist supports the regional implementation, roll-out and continuous improvement of the global compliance and privacy program across the Asia Pacific region. The role provides regional support and subject-matter expertise to strategic global compliance projects, core governance processes, and high-risk monitoring programs.

The global compliance program covers anti-corruption, health care compliance, Health Care Professional (HCP) interactions, ethical business practices, transparency reporting, medical device promotion, and privacy and data protection. The position acts as a primary point of contact to cross-functional leaders, drives program governance, and provides peer guidance, coaching, and direction on regional compliance matters drawing on prior knowledge of regional health care compliance and ethical business practices.

The role works closely with members of the Global Compliance Team, both the International Compliance team and the Global Operations team in the US and will partner with business functions in the identification and solution of compliance and privacy issues. The role reports directly to the Director of International Compliance and Global Privacy. The preferred base location for the position is Hong Kong or Singapore; other locations may be considered depending on experience.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS OF THE POSITION:

  • Assist in the implementation, roll out, and continuous improvement of the global compliance and privacy program across APAC (currently 10 geographies), to promote compliance with local laws, industry best practices and support business needs while maintaining global compliance standard processes.
  • Operate day-to-day regional compliance matters and escalate significant risks or complex issues to the Director of International Compliance and Global Privacy.
  • Support the deployment of the compliance program with guidance and support from the Global Compliance Team (International & US) while retaining responsibility for APAC field roll out and follow-through.
  • Apply prior knowledge of APAC compliance requirements and local business practices to identify regional risks, advise stakeholders, and translate global policies into practical and effective local controls and procedures.
  • Develop regional dashboards and reports that communicate key risks, monitoring results, emerging trends by geography (number is expected to increase), and remediation status to regional leadership and the global compliance team.
  • Monitor compliance requirements for HCP engagements, sponsorships, congresses, educational events, research and innovation forums, and marketing activities.
  • Localize, where needed, compliance policies, standards, and operating procedures for APAC geographies in coordination with Global Operations team, documenting local requirements and escalating conflicts with global compliance company standards.
  • Work on compliance education and practical guidance; adapt global materials for APAC audiences and languages and assist with the development and implementation of compliance training to employees and third parties and ultimately being responsible for the administration and monitoring of the compliance awareness program.
  • Support several compliance initiatives, including monitoring of transparency disclosures and related legal requirements across the regional markets and assisting in data collection for these requirements.
  • Act as a practical business partner who helps teams find compliant ways forward, offering timely advice and workable alternatives while maintaining clear compliance standards.
  • Provide compliance and data privacy general guidance and support to internal business partners.
  • Provide general support to the global compliance team as needed.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business, compliance, legal studies, finance, or a related field and at least 7 years of relevant experience, or an advanced degree and at least 5 years of relevant experience.
  • Proven hands-on experience in health care compliance in APAC markets, with a strong understanding of local business practices and industry codes of ethics and guidelines, such as JFMDA and AdvaMed China.
  • Experience in either medical devices, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, or another highly regulated industry; experience with HCP engagement oversight, grants, investigator-sponsored research, privacy, or data protection; and experience designing employee education curricula and measuring training effectiveness.
  • Communicate fluently in Mandarin and English, explain complex requirements clearly, present findings and recommendations, influence stakeholders, and facilitate training. Japanese language skills are preferred.
  • Proven hands-on experience in health care compliance in APAC markets and able to work independently.
  • Interpret complex requirements, use sound judgment to make practical, well-reasoned decisions in grey areas, and recognize when to seek specialist advice or escalate an issue.
  • Experience leading cross-functional projects and conducting monitoring, auditing, investigations, data analysis, risk assessments, and change management, with the ability to turn findings into practical improvements.
  • Use Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Outlook, and work with Power BI, Concur, or similar data, expense, payment, or workflow systems.
  • Demonstrate discretion with sensitive information, sound judgment, attention to detail, organization, business acumen, and problem-solving skills; prioritize competing duties, collaborate effectively, and deliver reliable work in a fast-paced environment.
  • Travel Internationally up to 20%.

What We Offer

With AtriCure, you'll get the opportunity to work with a team that is passionately dedicated to improving the lives of patients with Atrial Fibrillation worldwide. It is also a company that will invest in your professional development to help you grow and be successful in your role.

In Addition, AtriCure Also Provides:
The chance to work with an international team with more than 20 different nationalities, with 150+ international employees (on-site and in the field) which makes it a dynamic place to work.

The offer includes a competitive base salary, company bonus plan, mobility or Company car policy (depending on position), training and development opportunities, Paid annual leave, 2 days’ volunteer time off + 1 cultural heritage day per year, mental health support benefit, and dynamic company events.

Our Process

Please apply through LinkedIn or on our website. We would like to get to know you better so please feel free to share ample information about yourself and why you are interested in working with us. Once we have your application, our International Recruiter will contact you to find out more about your background and your expectations. The next steps include a meeting with the hiring manager to focus on key information about the role and to potential fit into the team. If this round is successful, you will get to meet a few of our team members to give you diverse perspectives about AtriCure. After all the interviews, we conduct reference checks to help us make the final decision.

description:

The YMCA of Greater Louisville strengthens communities through youth development, healthy living, and social responsibility. The Assistant Director of Kids Club & Family Events advances this mission by creating safe, welcoming, and engaging experiences that connect children and families to the Y.


This hands-on, part-time leadership position averages approximately 25 hours per week and combines direct care in Kids Club with activity planning, staff supervision, and family event coordination. The Assistant Director supports supervision of approximately 15 part-time staff, including teenage employees who may be entering the workforce for the first time.


Working closely with the Senior Director of Youth Development, the Assistant Director oversees daily program readiness, delivers age-appropriate activities, and coordinates family programs and celebrations. The Senior Director retains budget accountability, while the Assistant Director manages supplies and staffing within established guidelines.


Essential Responsibilities

  • Kids Club operations and direct care: Provide attentive care and active supervision of children. Follow check-in, check-out, health, safety, and supervision procedures. Keep program spaces, toys, and equipment clean, organized, safe, and ready for use.
  • Activity planning: Develop and implement a monthly calendar of age-appropriate crafts, games, and activities that engage children of different ages and abilities. Prepare materials and maintain adequate supplies.

title: Senior Manager – Operational Risk
location: Abu Dhabi Emirate, United Arab Emirates
description:
Summary


The Senior Manager – Operational Risk is responsible for developing, implementing, and enhancing the Bank's Operational Risk and Fraud Risk Management frameworks, with a strong focus on digital banking, emerging technologies, AI-enabled processes, and fraud prevention. The role will provide independent oversight and challenge to the business while supporting the safe growth of digital banking operations through proactive risk management, data-driven insights, and effective fraud controls.


The incumbent will work closely with Digital Banking, Technology, Operations, Product, Compliance, Internal Audit, and Business teams to strengthen the control environment, reduce operational losses, prevent fraud, and ensure compliance with regulatory expectations.


Key Responsibilities


Operational Risk Management


  • Lead the development, implementation, and enhancement of the Bank's Operational Risk Management Framework.
  • Identify, assess, monitor, and report operational risks across business, operational, digital, and technology functions.
  • Develop risk governance standards, methodologies, policies, and procedures aligned with regulatory expectations and industry best practices.
  • Provide oversight and challenge of operational risk assessments conducted across business units.
  • Monitor operational risk events, losses, near misses, control failures, and emerging risks.
  • Ensure timely identification and remediation of control weaknesses and operational vulnerabilities.
  • Review business processes, operating models, products, policies, outsourcing arrangements, and third-party relationships to identify operational risk exposures.
  • Track and monitor remediation actions arising from audits, regulatory reviews, risk assessments, and control reviews.


Digital Operational Risk


  • Establish risk oversight for digital banking platforms, customer onboarding processes, payment systems, lending platforms, and digital customer journeys.
  • Review technology-enabled processes and automation initiatives from an operational risk perspective.
  • Support the development of risk governance for AI-enabled, automated, and data-driven processes.
  • Assess risks arising from digital transformation initiatives, fintech partnerships, cloud-based environments, and emerging technologies.
  • Develop risk indicators and monitoring mechanisms for digital operations.


Fraud Risk Management


  • Develop and maintain the Bank's Fraud Risk Management Framework.
  • Lead fraud risk assessments across Customer onboarding, Digital banking channels, Payments and transfers, Lending activities, Cards and transaction banking and Internal fraud risks.
  • Develop fraud risk appetite metrics, policies, standards, and reporting frameworks.
  • Identify emerging fraud threats, fraud typologies, and vulnerabilities impacting the Bank.
  • Drive the implementation and enhancement of fraud monitoring, fraud detection, and fraud prevention capabilities.
  • Review fraud controls across digital and operational processes.
  • Analyze fraud incidents and loss events to identify root causes and strengthen preventive controls.
  • Work closely with business, compliance, and technology teams to improve fraud detection effectiveness.


Risk Analytics & Reporting


  • Develop management dashboards and reporting covering operational risk and fraud risk exposures.
  • Establish Key Risk Indicators (KRIs), loss metrics, fraud trends, and early warning indicators.
  • Utilize data analytics to identify risk patterns, trends, and emerging issues.
  • Prepare high-quality reports and presentations for Senior Management, Executive Committees, and Board Risk Committees.
  • Support data-driven decision-making through meaningful risk intelligence and insights.


Operational Resilience & Control Environment


  • Support the development of operational resilience capabilities across critical business services.
  • Assess operational dependencies, third-party risks, technology risks, and process vulnerabilities.
  • Strengthen control effectiveness across business and operational functions.
  • Promote continuous improvement in risk culture and control awareness across the organization.


Regulatory & Governance Responsibilities


  • Monitor regulatory developments relating to operational risk, fraud risk, operational resilience, digital banking, and emerging technologies.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable Central Bank and regulatory requirements.
  • Act as a trusted risk advisor to business and operational stakeholders.
  • Support regulatory reviews, inspections, and risk-related management responses.
  • Deliver risk awareness programs and training initiatives across the Bank.


Qualifications


  • Bachelor's Degree in Finance, Business Administration, Risk Management, Accounting, Economics, Technology, or a related discipline.
  • Master's Degree preferred.


Experience


  • Minimum 10 years of Operational Risk, Fraud Risk, Enterprise Risk, or related experience within banking, financial services, fintech, or digital banking environments.
  • Minimum 5 years in a managerial or leadership position.
  • Proven experience in developing and implementing Operational Risk and Fraud Risk frameworks.
  • Experience supporting digital banking operations, payment systems, customer onboarding, and technology-enabled business models.
  • Strong understanding of operational risk governance, fraud prevention, risk analytics, and regulatory expectations.
  • Experience engaging with senior management, regulators, auditors, and key stakeholders.

title: Manager, CXM Product Readiness
description:
About SimpliSafe

We’re a high-tech home security company that’s passionate about protecting the life you’ve built and our mission of keeping Every Home Secure. And we’ve created a culture here that cares just as deeply about the career you’re building. Ours is a no ego culture of collaboration and innovation where those seeking their next challenge can find big opportunities and make a huge impact on the lives of all those who we protect. We don’t just want you to work here. We want you to grow and thrive here.

We’re embracing a hybrid work model that enables our teams to split their time between office and home. Hybrid for us means we expect our teams to come together in our state-of-the-art office on two core days, typically Tuesday, Wednesday, or Thursday – working together in person and choosing where they work for the remainder of the week. We all benefit from flexibility and get to use the best of both worlds to get our work done.

Why are we hiring?

Well, we’re growing and thriving. So, we need smart, talented, and humble people who share our values to join us as we disrupt the home security space and relentlessly pursue our mission of keeping Every Home Secure.

What You'll Do

SimpliSafe is seeking a Manager to lead product readiness within Customer Experience & Monitoring (CXM). You will own the frameworks, cadences, and governance that prepare CXM for what's next, from product launches across hardware, firmware, app, monitoring, eCommerce, and marketing to the partner and operational work that supports them. You will lead a team and hold a portfolio of readiness work accountable for measurable performance and continuous improvement in core CXM KPIs, such as contact volume, repeat contact, and CSAT.

Primary Responsibilities Include:

  • Product Partnership & Design Feedback: Partner with Product and Engineering throughout the development cycle, providing direct feedback on designs and technical implementations to ensure features reflect CXM operational needs and protect core KPIs
  • Own the product readiness framework across CXM: Manage quarterly planning, intake, release cadences, and milestone reviews, and represent CXM across go/no-go conversations.
  • Maintain a forward view of upcoming launches and changes: Compile resource requirements so operational teams can plan capacity and sequencing.
  • Ensure launch readiness across frontline tooling, operations, and training: Verify that customer-facing content, channels, communications, and agent guidance and capacity are accounted for when changes go live.
  • Manage a portfolio of CXM readiness/product support, such as product readiness and vendor relationships: Establish goals, KPIs, and scorecards driving performance and continuous improvement against them.
  • Identify cross-functional risks and dependencies early: Escalate and drive resolution with stakeholders, translating readiness status, risks, and outcomes into clear takeaways for leadership.
  • Build standard processes, templates, RACIs, RAPIDs, and operating cadences: Scale across CXM to bring consistency to how readiness work runs.
  • Identify and implement opportunities to streamline and automate readiness operations with AI: Focus on reporting, intake, status, and cadences; set standards for team use; and measure the efficiency gained.
  • Lead, coach, and develop your team: Set priorities, clarify scope, ownership, KPIs, and build operating habits that foster team independence.

What You'll Bring

  • 5+ years of launch readiness, product operations, program management, or technical project management across software, mobile app, consumer product, or subscription ecosystems.
  • 2+ years of people management experience, leading and developing a team.
  • Proven record leading operational release readiness between product/engineering teams and customer service or contact center operations.
  • Track record managing a portfolio of initiatives to measurable outcomes in performance, efficiency, or customer experience, including defining KPIs, scorecards, and/or operating cadences.
  • Broad understanding of product lifecycle management as well as mobile ecosystem release cadences (iOS/Android app store processes, staging environments, beta testing, and feature flags).
  • Experience building cross-functional launch checklists and governance cadences, and coordinating ongoing work with project work.
  • Exceptional communication, influence, and cross-functional leadership skills, with comfort presenting to senior leadership and managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, Monday.com, and contact center / knowledge base platforms preferred.
  • Hands-on experience applying AI tools to streamline workflows, such as reporting, summarization, or process automation is preferred.

What Values You’ll Share

title: Senior Lead Security Engineer, Technology Resiliency
description:
Join the Firmwide Technology Resiliency group within JPMorganChase’s Cybersecurity & Technology Controls organization. The group ensures the firm’s technology estate can maintain effective operations and sustain the critical functioning of Essential Business Services against an evolving threat landscape. Our work underpins the firm's ability to meet global operational resilience expectations, helping to show regulators, clients and the business that critical services can withstand and recover from severe but plausible disruption.

We are seeking a Senior Lead Security Engineer to design and build product capabilities that operationalize the management of technology resiliency. This is a deeply hands-on engineering role: you will architect and write production code, set technical direction, and ship platforms consumed directly by operations and development teams across the firm. At the Senior Lead level, you are expected to own the technical strategy for a product area end-to-end - from problem framing and architecture through delivery, adoption, and operational ownership - while raising the engineering bar across adjacent teams.

Job responsibilities

  • Design, build, and evolve products that automate resilience management and give teams real-time insight into service health, dependencies, recovery readiness, and controls.
  • Combine telemetry, configuration, topology, change, and control evidence to identify resilience risks.
  • Automate resilience controls across software delivery, including policy checks, guardrails, evidence capture, and drift detection.
  • Generate and validate recovery plans from infrastructure templates and deployed environments, refreshing them as environments change.
  • Provide operational tools such as dashboards, control status views, exception and waiver workflows, recovery playbooks, and runbooks.
  • Automatically capture auditable resilience evidence—including dependency maps, recovery testing results, and control compliance—to support operational resilience and regulatory commitments.
  • Build data pipelines and models that represent service dependencies and resilience posture using graph-based approaches, including dependency graphs, blast-radius analysis, critical paths, and control coverage.
  • Develop analytics to identify risk concentration, single points of failure, configuration anti-patterns, and recovery-readiness gaps.
  • Apply site reliability engineering principles to improve product reliability, scalability, and operability through service level indicators and objectives, instrumentation, error budgets, and automation-first operations.
  • Lead by doing: contribute significant code while driving design reviews, technical direction, and delivery discipline.
  • Mentor engineers and raise standards across peer teams; partner with cyber operations, site reliability engineering, platform engineering, and risk stakeholders to define requirements, sequence delivery, and drive adoption.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • 7 years of professional experience in security engineering, site reliability engineering, production engineering or support, platform engineering, infrastructure reliability, or a related field.
  • Hands-on experience supporting, troubleshooting, or improving complex production environments, including building, shipping, or operating production systems.
  • Knowledge of security practices for production technology, including access controls, service accounts, network or service segmentation, platform security, or secure operations.
  • Proficiency in Python and SQL, with experience developing scripts, automation, or data solutions for engineering or operational use.
  • Experience with software or service design, including application programming interfaces, and with at least one additional programming language such as Rust, Java, JavaScript, or TypeScript.
  • Experience with cloud-native architecture, containers such as Docker or Kubernetes, and continuous integration and delivery practices.
  • Experience using infrastructure-as-code tools, such as Terraform, to manage infrastructure, environments, or configuration changes.
  • Understanding of secure software development practices and automated engineering controls in build and deployment pipelines.
  • Understanding of high-availability and disaster-recovery patterns across cloud or hybrid infrastructure.
  • Ability to explain technical designs, risks, and recommendations clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Cyber operations engineering background, including experience with security operations, cyber telemetry, detection engineering, cyber risk signals, or operational workflows.
  • Data science or analytics experience, particularly with graph technologies such as Neo4j, TigerGraph, or Amazon Neptune, including graph data modeling, query patterns, dependency mapping, and visualization.
  • Hands-on experience implementing policy-as-code or controls-as-code, including rules engines, pipeline gates, and automated evidence collection.
  • Experience generating and maintaining recovery and resilience plans from real infrastructure state, including infrastructure-as-code and runtime discovery, and embedding plans into operational workflows; familiarity with resilience frameworks such as DORA, UK PRA/FCA operational resilience, U.S. Interagency Sound Practices, FFIEC, Basel Principles, or NIST CSF.
  • Experience using AI-assisted development tools, such as GitHub Copilot or Claude Code, to accelerate delivery and improve developer productivity.
  • Proven ability to build collaborative partnerships with technical stakeholders, including technology vendor partners, and to work effectively in a matrixed organization.
  • Experience building and operating observability stacks and telemetry pipelines, including metrics, logs, traces, alerting, dashboards, and correlation and triage workflows; in-depth PaaS/IaaS virtualization knowledge, experience across multiple public cloud providers, or both.

title: Applied AI ML Executive Director
description:

Our mission is to deliver data, analytics, and AI that are secure and commercial to empower businesses to make better workforce decisions and enable enhanced employee experiences.

You set the technical agenda, direct the full research lifecycle across a portfolio of projects, and decide where to build, reuse, or partner — balancing fast, commercial delivery with stakeholder partnership and disciplined controls, across a global team.

Our team is building an artificial-intelligence-native operating environment — a template for how a global firm delivers artificial intelligence — which we intend to prove within our own organization before extending it more broadly. That work includes model factories that build and improve models against product benchmarks, a high-bandwidth evaluation factory that investigates edge cases and calibrates results, and agentic engineering tools deployed responsibly within a regulated environment. The guiding principle is to use AI to accelerate AI: invest in the tooling and infrastructure that let the team build and deliver faster. This role sets the vision and technical direction for that agenda and leads the people who carry it out.

Job responsibilities

  • Act as the hands-on leader of a team that delivers commercial outcomes using AI and machine learning solutions across our people-focused product areas
  • Direct the full research lifecycle, from framing problems and generating hypotheses through experiments, prototypes, and results that reach production
  • Develop model factories and a high-bandwidth evaluation factory that create, calibrate, and improve models and agents against product benchmarks
  • Advance agentic, specification-driven, and evaluation-driven development, including multi-agent orchestration deployed responsibly in a regulated environment
  • Translate models into insights that help reduce costs, expand capabilities, strengthen controls, and improve employee experiences
  • Promote reuse and partnership of techniques across the firm, and adopt vendor solutions where they add value
  • Partner with technology teams to architect scalable, cost-effective, enterprise-quality data and analytics systems, including self-service platforms

Keepro's client works with developers and construction professionals by using Building Information Modeling to engage in pro-active pre-construction programs that:

Looking to advance your construction leadership career at the forefront of digital construction and Virtual Design & Construction (VDC)? title: Principal Product Manager, Asset Intelligence
description:
Kai is the AI company rebuilding cybersecurity for the machine-speed era. Founded by second time founders and trusted by Fortune 500 enterprises, Kai is building a future where security has no categories, no silos, and no human speed bottlenecks. The Kai Agentic AI Platform replaces fragmented, human-limited workflows with agentic AI systems that continuously contextualize, assess, reason, and execute security work at machine speed - making human defenders, superhuman.

Why Join Kai

  • Well-funded: With $125M raised, we have the capital, runway, and resolve to rebuild cybersecurity from first principles.
  • Proven: We've earned the trust of Fortune 500 and Global 1000 companies, and we're just getting started. Their confidence in Kai reflects what we've built: an AI-powered cybersecurity platform that performs at the scale and speed the enterprise demands.
  • Experienced founders: Our founding team consists of second-time entrepreneurs, each with over 20 years of experience in the cybersecurity industry. Their proven expertise and vision drive our ambitious goals.
  • World-class leadership team: Our Heads of AI, Engineering, and Product bring extensive experience from some of the world’s most influential companies, ensuring top-tier mentorship, direction, and vision.
  • Frontier AI Applied Research Team: Our researchers operate at the leading edge of agentic AI systems, translating breakthrough capabilities into real-world cybersecurity applications.
  • Generous compensation: We offer highly competitive salaries, equity options, and a supportive work environment. Your contributions will be valued and rewarded as we grow together.

About the Role

We are looking for a Principal Product Manager to own asset intelligence at Kai. Every security decision depends on knowing what you have, what it runs, how it connects, and who is responsible for it, and most organizations cannot answer those questions. The same device appears several times across tools, the same software goes by different names, and nobody can say who owns what. Kai's asset intelligence layer builds a continuously updated, trustworthy picture of every asset, application, software package, relationship and owner, so that agents can decide what matters and act with confidence.

This is the foundation of Kai’s Autonomous Defense Platform, and of everything the platform does next: prioritization, routing, mitigation and automated remediation. It is a senior, hands-on role. You will set product direction, write the specs and drive releases, working directly with the Head of Product, the founders, Engineering, AI and Data Science, Design, Product Marketing, Sales and customers.

What You'll Do

  • Own the asset intelligence strategy and roadmap. Define the vision for a context graph of assets, software, applications, owners and relationships, and connect it to the outcomes it enables: risk-based prioritization, routing to the right owner, and safe automated action.
  • Define the connector strategy. Decide which sources matter (vulnerability scanners, EDR, cloud, IT management, CMDB, identity), how deep each integration goes, and how data freshness, quality and support status are managed. Prioritize by customer value and weigh build against partner.
  • Own asset identity resolution. Define how records from many tools are de-duplicated and merged into a common information model that keeps vendor-specific attributes. Set rules for confidence, conservative merging, explainability and correction when the system gets it wrong.
  • Own software identity. Build a canonical view of software: normalized names and versions, application grouping, SBOM and package data, and end-of-life and end-of-support status, so that questions like "who runs this product, and which version?" have one answer.
  • Run the product process. Write clear PRDs, prioritize ruthlessly, and own release readiness with Engineering, QA and Product Marketing using Kai’s lightweight product development lifecycle.
  • Partner on go-to-market. Work with Product Marketing and Sales on positioning, packaging (including how connectors are licensed) and enablement, and keep field messaging honest about what is shipped.
  • Raise the bar. Mentor other product managers and help shape how the product team operates as Kai scales.

What You Bring

  • 10+ years in product management, including 5+ years in enterprise security or IT products, ideally cyber asset attack surface management (CAASM), asset inventory, CMDB or IT asset management, vulnerability management, or exposure management.
  • Deep understanding of asset data: how scanners, EDR, cloud, device management and CMDB tools each describe the same asset, which identifiers are reliable, and why duplicates and gaps occur.
  • Experience with data-intensive platforms: entity resolution, data modeling, connectors and data pipelines, APIs, and ideally graph concepts.
  • Hands-on experience building or shipping products with AI and agentic workflows, with a practical view of evaluation, failure modes and guardrails.
  • A record of taking enterprise SaaS products from zero to one and scaling them, including multi-tenant and MSSP use cases.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, from crisp PRDs to executive-level narratives.
  • Comfort in a fast-moving startup: high ownership, a bias to ship, and willingness to wear several hats.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with CMDB or IT service management platforms, or with graph databases.
  • Familiarity with SBOM, software composition analysis and end-of-life data.
  • Prior experience at an early-stage company; MBA or equivalent business background.

Kai is an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, reproductive health decisions, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, genetic information, political views or activity, or other applicable legally protected characteristics.

title: Manager, Multiplatform Content and Audience Strategy
description:
Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Lead Multiplatform Content Strategy
  • Develop and execute newsroom strategy across broadcast, web, mobile, streaming, connected TV, social and emerging platforms.
  • Help determine the best platform, format and timing for our journalism rather than defaulting to a television-first approach.
  • Identify opportunities for streaming-exclusive, digital-first and platform-specific content.
  • Work with newsroom leadership to determine when major stories should move immediately to streaming or other platforms rather than waiting for the next television newscast.
  • Develop programming strategies that give audiences reasons to engage with NewsChannel 13 beyond our traditional newscasts.
Grow and Understand Our Audience
  • Use analytics and audience data to understand how people are finding, watching and interacting with our journalism.
  • Turn audience insights into actionable editorial and programming decisions.
  • Establish clear goals for audience growth, streaming consumption, engagement and multiplatform performance.
  • Identify opportunities to reach audiences who may rarely or never watch a traditional television newscast.
  • Monitor changing audience behaviors and emerging platforms and help determine where NewsChannel 13 should invest its time and resources.
Make Multiplatform Thinking Part of the Newsroom
  • Work with producers, reporters, anchors, photographers, meteorologists and managers to identify the best platform and presentation for each story.
  • Help journalists think beyond a single television package and develop content that works across multiple platforms.
  • Bring multiplatform strategy into editorial conversations from the beginning of the day, not after the television product is finished.
  • Develop workflows that allow the newsroom to move quickly on breaking and developing news without sacrificing accuracy or credibility.
  • Coach employees on multiplatform storytelling, audience strategy and platform best practices.
Strengthen Streaming and Digital Storytelling
  • Develop a consistent programming strategy for WNYT's streaming channels and connected-TV presence.
  • Create opportunities for original streaming programming around breaking news, weather, politics, investigations, community events and major Capital Region stories.
  • Build plans for extended live coverage when major news breaks.
  • Strengthen digital headlines, story presentation, SEO, video packaging, social distribution and short-form and vertical video.
  • Identify when stories deserve live blogs, explainers, extended interviews, data visualization, streaming specials or other alternative formats.
  • Evaluate what's working, what isn't and where we should experiment next.
Lead Smart Innovation
  • Serve as a newsroom resource for emerging platforms, technology and new storytelling tools.
  • Evaluate tools including AI-enabled newsroom technology, mobile production tools, audience analytics and content-management technology.
  • Test new workflows and ideas before expanding them across the newsroom.
  • Look beyond the broadcast industry for ideas about how audiences are consuming information.
  • Help us distinguish between meaningful innovation and the latest shiny object.

What Success Looks Like
Success in this position isn't simply publishing more stories or finding more places to put our television content.
It means:
  • More people discovering and engaging with NewsChannel 13 journalism.
  • Stronger and more consistent streaming programming.
  • Faster, smarter multiplatform coverage of breaking news.
  • More original content created specifically for streaming and digital audiences.
  • Better use of audience data in newsroom decision-making.
  • Reporters and producers considering multiple platforms from the beginning of the reporting process.
  • Continued growth in digital video, streaming and audience engagement.
  • A newsroom prepared for where local news consumption is going, not just where it has been.
The Opportunity
Local television is changing quickly. How audiences find news, when they consume it and the platforms they choose continue to evolve.
We don't want to simply react to those changes. We want to lead them.
As WNYT's Manager, Multiplatform Content and Audience Strategy, you'll help shape what the next generation of local journalism looks like at NewsChannel 13, combining the reporting, trust and community connection of a leading local newsroom with the speed, creativity and flexibility today's audiences expect.
The fundamental question behind this position is simple:
How do we make NewsChannel 13 essential to the Capital Region, no matter what screen our audience chooses?
If that's the kind of challenge that excites you, we want to hear from you.

The Peer Mentor utilizes relevant lived experience to foster positive relationships, promote participant engagement, encourage treatment adherence, assist with navigating community-based services, and support participants in achieving their individualized treatment, recovery, and personal goals. The Peer Mentor works collaboratively with clinical staff, Case Managers, and community-based providers to address barriers to participation and promote successful community integration. Peer Mentors provide services on an as-needed basis rather than maintaining an assigned caseload.
What are the key Responsibilities:
  1. Establish and maintain positive, trusting, and professional relationships with program participants, utilizing relevant lived experience to promote hope, recovery, self-advocacy, and personal accountability.
  2. Engage participants during program orientation and throughout their participation in the Felony ATI program.
  3. Provide individual peer support and facilitate educational, recovery-oriented, and supportive group discussions.
  4. Participate in service planning with clinical staff and Case Managers to support participants in achieving individualized treatment, supervision, and recovery goals.
  5. Utilize evidence-informed peer support and engagement strategies, consistent with training and scope of practice, to promote positive behavioral change and treatment engagement.
  6. Meet with participants on an ongoing, as-needed basis, both on and off site, and be available during assigned work hours via agency-approved telephone and email for support and guidance.
  7. Assist participants in connecting to community-based mental health and substance use treatment, recovery services, clubhouses, housing, benefits, educational and vocational opportunities, and other ancillary services.
  8. Accompany participants to appointments, treatment facilities, and community-based service providers when appropriate.
  9. Assist participants in identifying and addressing barriers to successful program participation, including transportation, housing, scheduling, communication, and access to community resources.
  10. Assist participants in completing program-related assignments, developing positive coping skills, and establishing prosocial support networks.
  11. Identify and communicate participant concerns, changes in presentation, engagement barriers, safety concerns, and additional service needs to assigned Case Managers, clinical staff, and supervision in a timely manner.
  12. Collaborate with program staff to reengage participants who are experiencing difficulties adhering to treatment or program requirements.
  13. Develop and maintain information regarding community-based recovery resources, peer support groups, and prosocial activities for distribution to program participants.
  14. Assist in developing and facilitating an alumni group to provide ongoing social and recovery support to individuals who have successfully completed the program.
  15. Maintain accurate and timely documentation of participant contacts, activities, referrals, and engagement efforts in UCMS, with records available for inspection by supervision at any time.
  16. Participate in case conferences, team meetings, regularly scheduled supervision, training, and continuous quality improvement activities.
  17. Maintain appropriate professional boundaries and participant confidentiality. Peer Mentors shall not independently conduct clinical assessments, provide therapy, render diagnoses, provide legal advice, or make recommendations to the Court.
  18. Perform all other relevant duties as determined by Supervision and EAC Network Administration.
What key knowledge, skills, and abilities are required to excel in this role:
Required:
  • High School Diploma or educational equivalent.
  • Relevant lived experience with recovery or navigating mental health, substance use, or criminal legal systems, and the ability to appropriately utilize that experience in a professional setting.
  • Demonstrated ability to engage and support individuals from diverse backgrounds in a respectful, nonjudgmental, and culturally responsive manner.
  • Good oral and written communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to maintain professional boundaries, exercise sound judgment, and adhere to confidentiality requirements.
  • Ability to work cooperatively with a multidisciplinary team, treatment providers, community-based organizations, and criminal legal system partners.
  • Knowledge of the needs of justice-involved individuals and available community resources.
  • Proficiency in computer applications and automated systems, including Microsoft Office, calendar, email, and electronic case management systems.
  • Ability to work in court, office, treatment provider, and community-based settings and travel throughout New York City.
  • Ability to comply with all Court access, identification, security, confidentiality, and facility requirements.
Preferred:
  • New York State Certified Recovery Peer Advocate (CRPA), Certified Peer Specialist (NYCPS), or equivalent peer support certification.
  • Experience providing peer support to justice-involved individuals with mental health, substance use, or co-occurring disorders.
  • Experience working in Alternatives to Incarceration, treatment courts, diversion, reentry, or other criminal legal settings.
  • Experience with group facilitation, motivational interviewing, recovery-oriented practices, and cognitive behavioral approaches within the scope of peer services.
  • Familiarity with New York City behavioral health, housing, benefits, employment, educational, and recovery resources.
  • Experience working with emerging young adults, older adults, and individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
  • Experience with UCMS or a comparable electronic case management system.
  • Bilingual English/Spanish a Plus!
What We Offer:
  • At EAC Network, you will find more than just a job – you will find a supportive work environment committed to your well-being and growth. We champion equity, justice, and belonging, fostering a workplace where every voice is valued and empowered.
  • We offer many roles with flexible and hybrid schedules to help you maintain a healthy work-life balance, and our generous PTO policy and Summer Fridays ensure you have time to recharge. Our commitment to wellness also earned us the Gold Healthy Workforce Designation from Cigna in 2024 and 2025.
  • Additionally, all employees are eligible to participate in EAC Network’s 401(k) plan, and full-time employees receive a 3% employer contribution after one year of service. EAC employees may also be eligible for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. At EAC Network, you are part of a team making a difference in our communities across Long Island and New York City, every day.

title: Thermal Engineer
description:
Gencor is seeking an experienced Thermal Engineer to support the design, analysis, optimization, and troubleshooting of thermal and combustion systems used in asphalt production and heavy industrial equipment manufacturing. The ideal candidate will bring strong expertise in heat transfer, combustion systems, airflow dynamics, and industrial process heating while working closely with mechanical, electrical, and controls engineering teams.

This role is critical in improving equipment efficiency, combustion performance, emissions compliance, and overall plant reliability across asphalt production systems.


RELOCATION ASSISTANCE AVAILABLE.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and optimize thermal systems utilized in asphalt plants and heavy industrial equipment, including burners, dryers, combustion chambers, heat exchangers, and related process heating equipment.
  • Perform thermal and airflow analysis to improve heat transfer efficiency, fuel consumption, and production performance.
  • Troubleshoot combustion and thermal system issues in both manufacturing and field environments.
  • Support burner tuning, flame optimization, and emissions reduction initiatives.
  • Collaborate with controls engineers on combustion controls, instrumentation, PLC integration, and burner management systems.
  • Conduct thermal performance testing and assist with commissioning and startup activities at customer job sites as needed.
  • Develop engineering calculations, technical specifications, and supporting documentation.
  • Partner with manufacturing and service teams to resolve field issues and implement product improvements.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable safety, environmental, and industry standards including NFPA and emissions regulations.
  • Participate in continuous improvement efforts focused on equipment reliability, efficiency, and product innovation.


Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or related engineering discipline.
  • 5+ years of experience with industrial thermal systems, combustion equipment, process heating, or asphalt plant equipment.
  • Strong understanding of thermodynamics, heat transfer, combustion principles, and fluid dynamics.
  • Experience working with industrial burners, rotary dryers, asphalt plants, aggregate equipment, or similar heavy industrial systems preferred.
  • Familiarity with combustion controls, PLC systems, instrumentation, and burner management systems (BMS).
  • Ability to troubleshoot complex thermal and combustion performance issues.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Willingness to travel occasionally for field support, commissioning, and customer site visits.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience within asphalt, aggregate, or heavy equipment manufacturing industries
  • Knowledge of natural gas, propane, or fuel oil combustion systems
  • Experience with emissions reduction and fuel efficiency optimization
  • Familiarity with AutoCAD, SolidWorks, or thermal modeling software
  • Understanding of NFPA, OSHA, and environmental compliance standards


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Competitive salary based on experience
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance
  • 401(k) with company match
  • Paid time off and company holidays

title: UX Creative Technologist, Vice President

  • Integrate AI natively into daily workflows — including prototyping, concept generation, testing and specification.

  • Support training sessions, documentation and collateral to onboard designers, content writers and researchers into new tooling and ways of working.

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

title: Vocational Rehab Evaluator
description:
Overview

DePaul’s WorkGuide Program offers a wide range of pre-employment and employment services to Monroe County residents who qualify for Adult Career and Continuing Education Services-Vocational Rehabilitation (ACCES-VR). The Vocational Rehab Evaluator will provide pre-employment, potentially eligible, and placement services to adults and students referred through ACCES-VR as well as through Community Providers and/or School Districts. The Vocational Rehab Evaluators will provide vocational assessments, facilitate classes, and develop community-based work experiences to further assess customers’ work readiness while identifying accommodations prior to seeking competitive employment. Ideal candidates will hold a bachelor’s degree in vocational Rehabilitation Counseling, Career Counseling, or a related field, will be well-organized, resourceful, and committed to helping individuals achieve meaningful employment outcomes. Strong verbal and written communication skills, the ability to work independently with minimal supervision, and proficiency in computer use are required. A flexible work schedule is required to provide coaching support during interviews and/or on-site job coaching at worksites if/when customers’ work schedules are outside of WorkGuide office hours. Vocational Rehab Evaluators must have previous experience providing vocational rehabilitation services funded through ACCES-VR, Office of Mental Health, OPWDD, Commission for the Blind, or other County/State Vocational Rehabilitation Programs.

Why work for DePaul?

  • Make a positive difference in someone's life
  • Supportive work environment
  • We value diversity
  • Opportunity for professional development and career advancement
  • Excellent benefits and competitive wages
  • Pay range for this position is $25.50-$26.40/hour

Responsibilities

  • Respects and maintains customer’s rights and confidentiality and demonstrates a positive caring attitude toward all consumers, staff, guests and service providers.
  • Provide oversight of ACCES-VR funded Core Rehabilitation Services.
  • Provide Community outreach and market vocational programs to referral agents.
  • Conduct vocational assessments; prepare and present comprehensive assessment with recommendations to participants and their stakeholders.
  • Provide one-to-one vocational counseling and make recommendations based on findings.
  • Facilitate vocational classes.
  • Provide development for unpaid work experience &/or competitive job placements.
  • Conduct site visits as necessary to assess progress, identify accommodations, and meet regulatory criteria.
  • Job coaching as necessary to maximize the success of unpaid work experience &/or job placements.
  • Responsible for tracking and submitting billing and ACCES-VR milestone reports and monthly reports.
  • Must develop good working relationships with all stakeholders including but not limited to ACCES-VR, Community Businesses, High School Personnel, family members, therapists, Medicaid Service Coordinators, Case Manager, etc.
  • Must adhere to WorkGuide procedures and regulations.
  • Role model professional workplace behaviors, professional boundaries, and code of conduct in the office and community settings.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by supervisor to meet fluctuating referral and program needs.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Vocational Rehabilitation, Career Counseling or related field and two years of experience conducting vocational assessment &/or vocational rehabilitation services, or a combination of education and experience approved by ACCES-VR prior to final job offer.
  • Experience working with adults and/or youth with disabilities including but not limited to DD, LD, CD, MH, blind/ low vision, and/or deaf or hard of hearing.
  • Previous experience should include conducting vocational assessment services, job coaching, and/or developing work experience/internships/job placements with community-based employers.
  • Must have good communication skills, both verbal and written.
  • ASL is a plus but is not required.
  • Must be well organized and be able to work with limited supervision.
  • Must be computer literate with the ability to learn/utilize required technology (Microsoft, Outlook, TEAMS, Zoom, AWARDS, ADP/DOCEBO, Smartlinx, etc.)
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule around program needs and customers’ employment needs.
  • Must have a current, clean/valid NYS driver’s license that meets the agency’s clean driving record policy.
  • Must have reliable transportation and vehicle to perform job duties.

Benefits

This position is eligible for the following benefits: Medical Insurance, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life Insurance, Generous PTO & Paid Holidays, 403B Employer Match, and Employee Discount Programs.

DePaul is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity. All employment is decided based on qualifications, merit and program need.

title: Director of Financial Planning - Delos
description:
ROLE MANDATE

Own financial planning across both Delos platforms. Serve as the senior planning practitioner and team leader for Delos Private Client Group's comprehensive, goals-based planning practice, while building the standardized, technology-enabled financial planning program that Delos Wealth Advisors will consistently lead with — a lighter-touch offering by design, but one every Wealth Advisor is expected to deliver and be monitored against. This role sets the planning standard for the entire Delos Wealth franchise; it does not carry sales production credit or AUM/P&L accountability, which sit with the Wealth Sales and Trust Sales leadership roles.

The Opportunity

Delos Private Client Group and Delos Wealth Advisors have the fiduciary infrastructure and institutional backing to become a premier, planning-led wealth management franchise across Texas and Oklahoma. Delos Private Client Group already delivers deep, comprehensive financial planning to high-net-worth households. Delos Wealth Advisors — operating across third-party broker-dealer, RIA, and insurance platforms — needs a consistent, repeatable planning discipline it can lead with in every client conversation, without requiring the same depth of resourcing as the Private Client Group practice.

This role is built for a practitioner-leader who can operate at both altitudes: hands-on, senior-level planning for complex Private Client Group households, and program design, technology governance, and adoption monitoring for a much broader population of Wealth Advisors.

Position Purpose

Own financial planning quality and consistency across Delos Wealth by (1) leading, mentoring, and elevating the Delos Private Client Group planning team and its comprehensive planning practice, and (2) building, deploying, and monitoring adherence to a standardized financial planning program for Delos Wealth Advisors — delivered through eMoney, MoneyGuidePro, or a comparable platform — so that every Wealth Advisor leads with a defined planning experience, regardless of practice size or complexity.

Role Scope

The Role Owns

  • Comprehensive financial planning strategy, quality, and team leadership for Delos Private Client Group
  • Design, rollout, and ongoing governance of the standardized Delos Wealth Advisors financial planning program
  • Selection, configuration, and administration of financial planning technology platforms (eMoney, MoneyGuidePro, or comparable) across both entities
  • Monitoring, reporting, and enforcement of Wealth Advisor adherence to the required minimum planning standard
  • Review and approval of financial plans prepared by junior Private Client Group planners

The Role Does Not Own

  • Sales production credit, AUM growth targets, or P&L accountability for Wealth Strategists and Wealth Advisors (owned by the Head of Wealth Sales)
  • Trust origination, fiduciary acceptance, or trust administration (owned by Trust Services and the Head of Trust Sales & Business Development)
  • Portfolio construction or investment management decisions
  • Recruiting, coaching, or performance management of advisors related to production performance (a Wealth Sales responsibility, though findings may be shared collaboratively)
  • Day-to-day supervision of individual Wealth Advisors' practices outside of the planning program

Primary Responsibilities

Delos Private Client Group — Comprehensive Planning Leadership

  • Serve as a senior planner on complex, high-net-worth client engagements requiring advanced planning expertise across retirement, tax, estate, cash flow, insurance, and investment strategy
  • Lead, mentor, and grow the Private Client Group's team of financial planners and associate advisors
  • Establish and maintain firm-wide planning standards, workflows, and best practices for comprehensive plans
  • Review and approve financial plans prepared by junior planners to ensure accuracy and alignment with client goals
  • Drive a consistent, repeatable planning process that scales with Private Client Group growth while preserving personalization

Delos Wealth Advisors — Financial Planning Program Design & Oversight

  • Design a standardized, lighter-touch financial planning program that every Delos Wealth Advisor is expected to lead client relationships with, appropriately scoped to the broker-dealer, RIA, and insurance channels they operate in
  • Define the minimum planning deliverable, workflow, and cadence for Wealth Advisors, and the criteria that trigger escalation to a full Private Client Group comprehensive plan
  • Build training, templates, and enablement materials so Wealth Advisors can deliver the program consistently at scale
  • Monitor and report on Wealth Advisor adherence to the planning program, identifying gaps and working with the Program Manager on remediation
  • Refine the program on an ongoing basis based on adoption data, advisor feedback, and client outcomes

Technology & Platform Management

  • Own selection, configuration, and administration of the financial planning platform(s) — eMoney Advisor, MoneyGuidePro, or comparable — across Delos Private Client Group and Delos Wealth Advisors
  • Establish the system of record and reporting cadence used to monitor Wealth Advisor plan creation, completion, and adherence
  • Collaborate with operations and compliance to ensure planning processes and technology use meet regulatory standards across both platforms
  • Develop reporting and analytics that track planning quality and capacity at Private Client Group and planning-program adoption at Wealth Advisors

Strategy & Cross-Platform Collaboration

  • Partner with the Chief Investment Officer of Delos Private Client Group to define and execute the planning department's strategic roadmap
  • Work closely with the Program Manager of Delos Wealth Advisors to align the planning program with the broader Wealth Advisors operating model and advisor experience
  • Coordinate with the Director of Wealth Sales and Director of Trust Sales & Business Development so planning findings feed appropriately into sales, referral, and Trust conversations without crossing into their production ownership
  • Stay current on financial planning trends, tax law changes, and regulatory developments affecting client strategies across both platforms
  • Support new client acquisition by participating in prospect meetings and articulating the value of Delos's planning approach when appropriate

Success Measures

Private Client Group Planning Quality

  • Comprehensive plans delivered and reviewed
  • Plan accuracy and completeness
  • Client and advisor satisfaction with the planning process

Wealth Advisors Program Adoption

  • Percentage of Wealth Advisors actively using the required planning program
  • Plans initiated and completed per advisor
  • Time to first plan for newly onboarded advisors

Program Governance

  • Adherence rate to the defined minimum planning standard
  • Frequency and resolution of adherence gaps
  • Escalations to full comprehensive planning

Technology & Reporting

  • Platform utilization across both entities
  • Reliability and timeliness of adherence and quality reporting
  • Data quality within the planning system of record

Team Development

  • Private Client Group planners mentored and developed
  • Quality of plans reviewed and approved
  • Bench strength for future growth

Cross-Platform Alignment

  • Effectiveness of partnership with the CIO, Program Manager, Wealth Sales, and Trust Sales leadership
  • Quality of referrals and hand-offs generated from planning conversations

Required

Qualifications and Experience

  • CFP® designation (CERTIFIED FINANCIAL PLANNER™) required
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience in comprehensive financial planning
  • Deep expertise in retirement income planning, tax planning strategies, estate planning concepts, and investment planning
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and develop planning teams in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment
  • Hands-on experience with eMoney Advisor, MoneyGuidePro, or comparable financial planning software, including platform administration
  • Series 65 (or 66) license, or ability to obtain within 90 days of hire
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex financial concepts for diverse audiences and skill levels

Preferred

  • Advanced credentials such as CPA, CFA, CEPA, CPWA, ChFC, or Legal Degree
  • Experience designing or standardizing a financial planning program across a multi-channel advisor population (RIA, broker-dealer, and/or insurance)
  • Experience working within an RIA, independent broker-dealer, or fee-only advisory environment
  • Familiarity with the Oklahoma and/or Texas wealth management market
  • Experience monitoring advisor adherence, compliance, or quality standards at scale
  • Background in business owner planning, executive compensation, or trust and estate strategies
  • Prior experience reporting to or partnering with a CIO and a separate advisor-platform Program Manager

The Right Fit — And the Wrong One

You will thrive here if...

  • You enjoy operating at two altitudes — deep, technical planning work and broad program design
  • You want to set the planning standard for an entire advisor population, not just your own clients
  • You're comfortable owning adherence and quality monitoring without owning sales production or AUM targets
  • You think in systems, templates, and technology as much as in individual client plans
  • You're energized by partnering across a CIO and a separate Program Manager to align two distinct platforms

This role is not the right fit if...

  • You only want to do one-on-one planning work and have no interest in building a scalable program
  • You expect every advisor to deliver the same depth of plan as the Private Client Group practice
  • You want AUM, P&L, or sales-production accountability — that sits with Wealth Sales
  • You prefer to avoid technology administration and platform governance work
  • You prefer a single reporting line and a narrowly defined book of clients

How The Role Fits Within Delos Wealth

title: Inventory Supervisor - Tracy, CA

  • Ability to communicate clearly and concisely, both written and oral.
  • Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.
  • Ability to multitask and prioritize effectively.
  • Ability to resolve complex issues with guidance from others.
  • Ability to work overtime and on weekends.
  • Ability to work variable schedule(s) as necessary.

Of course, we’ll make any reasonable accommodations for those with disabilities to perform the essential functions of their jobs.

What we’ll offer in return

description:

As a Product Manager at JPMorganChase within the Home Lending Product Transformation team, you will own the delivery of AI-enabled solutions that drive measurable outcomes across the home lending journey.   • Partner with engineering, design, data science, and business stakeholders to shape scalable AI solutions, communicate trade-offs clearly, and drive fast, well-informed decisions across teams
  • Identify and pursue opportunities to apply AI and automation to eliminate manual work, reduce cycle time, and reimagine legacy processes across the home lending ecosystem
  • Champion a culture of experimentation and continuous improvement, challenging legacy approaches and leading cross-functional initiatives that raise the bar for what AI-powered products can deliver

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Formal training or certification on product engineering concepts and 5+ years applied experience
  • Hands-on experience shipping AI-powered or agentic capabilities end-to-end, including tool-using orchestration workflows, prompt engineering, and practical model evaluation and grounding approaches
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver agentic task-automation solutions that streamline end-to-end workflows—including exceptions and human handoffs—and produce measurable outcomes such as cycle-time reduction, productivity gains, or improved customer satisfaction
  • Advanced product analytics capability with the ability to set outcome targets, instrument features, and manage delivery to quantified results; experience applying AI and machine learning within governance frameworks to enhance discovery, prioritization, and customer experience decisions
  • Strong ability to translate business strategy into functional specifications and integration-ready requirements, including data definitions, business rules, and non-functional requirements for AI-powered systems

title: Principal Electrochemical Engineer
description:
Principal Electrochemical Engineer

Location: Austin, Texas | Fully Onsite – No Remote or Hybrid


Company Overview

An innovative water technology company developing advanced purification and treatment systems for industrial, municipal, and commercial applications. The organization is focused on bringing next-generation electrochemical technologies to market, improving treatment efficiency, reducing operating costs, and advancing water reuse capabilities.


As the company continues to grow, it is looking for an experienced electrochemical engineer to help lead technology development and commercial scale-up.


Position Overview

The Principal Electrochemical Engineer will lead the design, development, testing, and commercialization of advanced electrochemical treatment systems.

This individual will take ownership of reactor design, electrode development, system optimization, and scale-up from laboratory testing through pilot and commercial deployment.

The ideal candidate has strong fundamentals in electrochemistry and a proven track record of translating research and development into practical, real-world applications. This is a hands-on technical leadership role working closely with mechanical, electrical, process, and manufacturing engineering teams.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the design and development of electrochemical reactors, cells, electrodes, and treatment systems.
  • Evaluate electrode materials, coatings, corrosion resistance, and long-term system durability.
  • Investigate electrochemical reactions, kinetics, contaminant removal, and treatment efficiency.
  • Conduct laboratory testing and apply electroanalytical techniques to improve system performance.
  • Develop simulation and modeling tools using COMSOL, ANSYS, or similar platforms.
  • Drive technology scale-up from laboratory prototypes to pilot and commercial systems.
  • Support equipment testing, validation, commissioning, and field troubleshooting.
  • Collaborate with electrical and manufacturing teams on power delivery, system integration, and production readiness.
  • Establish testing procedures, technical documentation, and operational guidelines.
  • Mentor engineering personnel and contribute to the company's technology development roadmap.


Required Qualifications

  • PhD in Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electrochemistry, Materials Science, or a related field. Master's degree candidates with equivalent experience will be considered.
  • 8+ years of relevant experience in electrochemical engineering, applied research, or technology development.
  • Demonstrated experience taking electrochemical technologies from laboratory development through pilot or commercial scale.
  • Strong understanding of electrochemical principles, including kinetics, thermodynamics, mass transport, and electrode performance.
  • Hands-on experience with electrochemical testing equipment, potentiostats, and galvanostats.
  • Knowledge of electrode materials, coatings, corrosion, and degradation mechanisms.
  • Experience with COMSOL, ANSYS, Python, MATLAB, or similar engineering tools.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools and engineering automation.
  • Strong technical communication and independent problem-solving skills.


Preferred Experience

  • Experience commercializing electrochemical technologies within a startup or R&D environment.
  • Background in multiphase flow, gas generation, and CFD modeling.
  • Experience with corrosion science and materials selection.
  • Familiarity with instrumentation, LabVIEW, PLC/SCADA, and automated testing systems.
  • Knowledge of water treatment, water reuse, and relevant industry standards.

title: Transactions Specialist IV - Exceptions Processing Team
description:

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage aging/work-in-progress
  • Excel proficiency (non-negotiable): pivot tables, filters/sorts, and formulas (e.g., XLOOKUP/VLOOKUP, IF, SUMIFS/COUNTIFS); able to work with large datasets
  • Strong computer proficiency across common programs and systems (Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, web navigation, file management); beyond basic
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Schedule: Monday – Friday 6:30am-3:30pm

title: Wholesale Credit Risk - London - 2027 ReEntry Program
description:

title: Senior Transportation Project Manager
description:

Dewberry is seeking a Senior Transportation Project Manager in our Orlando, FL office. Dewberry has provided planning and design services to FDOT, municipal agencies, and toll authorities throughout Florida for decades and has a strong backlog of work, with current projects in good standing that are ready to be transitioned as part of our succession planning. Whether you’re an experienced professional or a new graduate, you’ll have the chance to collaborate with the best and brightest and work on innovative and complex projects at the forefront of the industry.   • A long-established Florida transportation practice with successful project histories at agencies across the state, a steady backlog of ongoing projects, and a strong pipeline in place to win future projects
  • The resources of a large firm, such as access to national subject matter experts, the ability to effectively workshare across offices/geographies, and systems/people in place that support our marketing, accounting, and recruiting functions
  • A variety of opportunities – our projects range from major highway widenings & new construction to innovative intersections & interchanges to trails & safety improvements. Our client base is diversified between FDOT, CFX, counties across the state, and Contractor teams constructing large design-build projects.
  • Competitive compensation and benefits packages, numerous formal training programs, and clear opportunities for growth in technical, project management, and organizational management career paths

Responsibilities

  • Lead the delivery of complex transportation design projects and oversee the preparation of deliverables by project teams
  • Manage project quality, scopes, schedules, budgets, and risks from the initial pursuit phase through design and construction
  • Collaborate closely with other Project Managers and Transportation Discipline Leaders

Required Skills & Required Experience

  • Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering or a related field and a Florida Professional Engineer (PE) license

Make an Impact

If you're an experienced project manager looking for the opportunity to work with an outstanding team delivering impactful infrastructure projects while building your reputation with clients, we'd love to talk with you.
